cls: Centrally acting skeletal muscle relaxant (antispasticity / antispastic agent)
quick: 50 mg three times daily after meals (usual total 150 mg/day)
Safety not established; use only if clearly necessary
Avoid - excreted in animal milk; if needed, stop breastfeeding
Use with caution; rare hepatic dysfunction reported - monitor LFTs
Avoid - additive drowsiness and CNS effects
Drowsiness, weakness, liver function with prolonged use; signs of hypersensitivity
summary: Eperisone hydrochloride is a centrally acting skeletal muscle relaxant used for painful muscle spasm associated with musculoskeletal disorders (e.g., low back pain, cervical spondylosis, periarthritis) and for spasticity from neurological disorders (e.g., after stroke, cervical spondylosis, cerebral palsy). It relaxes both skeletal and vascular smooth muscle, reducing myotonia, improving circulation, and suppressing the pain reflex. It is not approved by the US FDA but is widely used in Japan, India, and other countries.
indications: Symptomatic relief of muscle spasm associated with musculoskeletal disorders (low back pain, cervical/shoulder-arm syndrome, periarthritis)

Spastic paralysis due to neurological disease (cerebrovascular disease, cervical spondylosis, spinal cord injury, cerebral palsy, post-surgical/traumatic sequelae, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and other spinal/cerebral disorders)

dosage.d: 50 mg three times daily after meals (150 mg/day)
dosage.n: Adjust according to age and symptom severity; typical course 7-14 days for acute spasm

admin: Take after meals to reduce gastrointestinal upset
Adjust dose based on age and symptom response
Avoid activities requiring alertness (driving, operating machinery) until effects are known
Avoid concomitant alcohol and other sedatives
moa: Eperisone is a centrally acting muscle relaxant. It acts on the spinal cord and skeletal muscle spindles to reduce muscle tone, relaxing both skeletal and vascular smooth muscle. Its effects include reduction of myotonia (muscle stiffness), improvement of local blood circulation, and suppression of the pain reflex, thereby breaking the cycle of pain, spasm, and ischemia.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to eperisone or any component of the formulation
relative: Patients performing tasks requiring full alertness (risk of drowsiness/weakness)

preg: The safety of eperisone in pregnancy has not been established. It should be used during pregnancy only if the expected therapeutic benefit clearly outweighs the potential risk.
lact: Eperisone is excreted in the milk of lactating animals; use during breastfeeding should be avoided. If treatment is essential, breastfeeding should be discontinued.
renal: Specific data in renal impairment are limited; use with caution and monitor for adverse effects.
hepatic: Use with caution. Rare cases of hepatic dysfunction/elevated liver enzymes have been reported; monitor liver function during prolonged therapy and discontinue if abnormalities occur.

moderate: Methocarbamol and other CNS depressants/muscle relaxants (additive effects; reports of visual accommodation disturbance)
Alcohol, sedatives, hypnotics, anxiolytics (additive CNS depression/drowsiness)
minor: Tolperisone and similar centrally acting relaxants (additive muscle weakness)
interactions.food: Take after meals; food reduces GI upset
interactions.alcohol: Avoid - additive drowsiness and impaired coordination
interactions.diagnostics: May rarely cause elevated liver enzymes; monitor LFTs with prolonged use

serious: Hepatic dysfunction with elevated liver enzymes / jaundice
rare: Toxic epidermal necrolysis / severe skin reactions

monitoring: Degree of drowsiness and muscle weakness
Liver function tests during prolonged treatment
Renal function and blood counts if symptoms suggest
Signs of hypersensitivity or severe skin reaction
counsel: Take after meals; this medicine can make you drowsy or weak, so do not drive or operate machinery until you know how it affects you
Avoid alcohol and other sedating medicines
Stop the medicine and seek care if you develop rash, swelling, difficulty breathing, or yellowing of the skin/eyes
Report persistent weakness, dizziness, or unusual tiredness
Use it for the prescribed duration; it relieves muscle spasm and associated pain
pk: Symptomatic muscle relaxation within hours of dosing
Plasma peak approximately 1.6 to 1.9 hours after an oral dose
Store at controlled room temperature; protect from light and moisture
pearls: NOT FDA-approved; widely used in Japan, India, and parts of Asia/Europe as a centrally acting muscle relaxant (data here reflect SmPC/manufacturer and BNF-type sources)
Less sedating than many other centrally acting relaxants, but drowsiness and weakness still occur - caution with driving
Dual action on skeletal and vascular smooth muscle improves local circulation and breaks the pain-spasm cycle
Monitor liver function on prolonged use; rare serious hypersensitivity (anaphylactoid shock, severe skin reactions) has been reported
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and continue your regular schedule - do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Experience with overdose is limited. Expect exaggerated effects such as marked drowsiness, muscle weakness, hypotonia, dizziness, and gastrointestinal upset. Management is symptomatic and supportive (airway, breathing, circulation); there is no specific antidote.
